name: Université Laval - Diploma program
overview:
ADDITIONAL PROGRAMME SPECIFICS

  • Programme fee of 15 000€ for non French/Belgian nationalities


LAVAL UNIVERSITY

The university has nearly 40,000 students from over 110 countries. It is ranked among the ten largest research universities in Canada and is the first French-speaking university in America. It’s a very prestigious university.

Located in Quebec City, recognized as a UNESCO World Heritage Site, the University of Laval offers a lively cultural, sporting and social life with many activities and amenities.

It has over 500 different programs for all kind of studies and is one of the hearts of the intellectual ecosystem of Québec.

The campus, which is 1.8 km square wide, is dotted with great architecture, greenery and woods. It has a modern sports complex, among the most impressive in the country, as well as numerous hiking trails and underground walkways.


To find out more on advice to travelers issued by the Ministry of Europe and Foreign Affairs on the host country, click here
administrative:
1. Application dossier

You will work directly with the partner university regarding your application. All required documents will have to be uploaded on their platform or sent by email before the deadline (see the Americas Teams channel for each application deadline).

If you have not received anything yet, it means your nomination has not been sent yet, please be patient.


To be given to Epitech bachelor campus administration to reenroll for the Tech4 (in April/May):

  • The addendum to the contract.
  • EPITECH re-registration dossier.


This information is subject to change by the partner university. They will provide you with the most current information upon your acceptance.


Documents you will need to take with you:

- Certified copies of the bachelor's degree and the transcript of the bachelor

- CAQ and proof of obtaining a study permit


Please note : upon arrival, you will be asked to provide official copies of all transcripts and diplomas obtained (i.e. your baccalaureate diploma and transcript) at the Office of the Registrar.


This information is subject to change by the partner university. They will provide you with the most current information upon your acceptance.

Additionally, please note that there are additional tuition fees on the side of the partner university that you need to take into account: 2 900€ for French and Belgian students and 15 000€ for non-French and non-Belgian students.


2. Visa

The steps must be taken at the green light from the University, because the procedures can take a long time. Check out updated information directly on the university's website. Once you have your admission letter in hand, you must obtain:

  • the Quebec Acceptance Certificate for studies (CAQ) , issued by the government of Quebec (At the expense of the student : 124$ CA). The application of the CAQ for studies must be done online and it takes approximatively 6 weeks to be issued.The steps to apply for the CAQ:
  • Once you have received your admission letter, follow these steps and apply online: www.immigration-quebec.gouv.qc.ca/en/electronic-services/caq-electronic/index.html
  • Complete the online CAQ application
  • Print: declaration and commitment form (must be signed) and the personalized checklist
  • Review and ensure you have the appropriate support documents – remember to include ALL pages of your Offer of Admission.


We boldly recommend that you mail your application package with all supporting documents by express mail to the address indicated on the personalized checklist.

Note: Whether you apply online or mail your application, you must mail the required documents to MIFI's Montréal office, regardless of your current place of residence. Your application will not be considered until all supporting documents have been received, so don't delay. Processing time is 4 to 8 weeks!


  • The bank letter in French will be required for the CAQ request (see corresponding paragraph below). As an indication, the amount requested amount is around 24 617$ CAD in 2026.
  • Please follow the sample letter available by clicking here . For the tuition fees, you will pay those of Epitech.


PLEASE NOTE: if the bank letter is not in your name but that of your parents, for example, you must attach the declaration of financial support (you must also attach it for the CAQ request): http: // www .immigration-quebec.gouv.qc.ca / publications / fr / etudes / D09.pdf


  • the study permit, issued by Immigration, Refugees, and Citizenship Canada - IRCC (Cost to be borne by the student: 150 $ CA + 85$ for biometrics fee). Once you have received the electronic version of your CAQ, immediately apply for your Study Permit. The application must be done online on the IRCC website. This study permit application automatically includes a visa or Electronic Travel Authorization (eTA) at no additional cost. Apply online: https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/study-canada/study-permit/apply.html


  • The IRCC website allow you to pay fees related to the study permit application, apply for the study permit, verify the status of your application.
  • The estimated time for the process is 12 weeks.


  • Go to this website to see the study permit application process : Guide 5269 – Présenter une demande de permis d’études de l‘extérieur du Canada - Canada.ca


  • Citizens of all countries except the United States and other minor exceptions have to give their biometrics in order to obtain a visa or permit.
  • In the hours following submission of your online application, you will receive the 'instruction letter' in your MyCIC account with instructions to submit your biometrics at a collection service point. For more information, just click here: https://www.cic.gc.ca/francais/information/ou-fournir-donnees-biometriques.asp


  • Students who reside or have resided for six months or more in the past year in certain countries need a medical exam by a IRCC-approved physician. You should allow at least one month for this process, and you are responsible for the cost of the exam. The embassy that handles your case will contact you and provide instructions as needed.


  • Citizens of certain countries must obtain a temporary resident visa (TRV) or electronic travel authorization (eTA) from Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada (IRCC) to be able to enter Canada. The visa is placed directly in your passport, whereas the eTA is electronically linked to your passport. Your application for a study permit made outside Canada automatically includes a visa or an eTA at no additional cost.


  • You will receive confirmation that the study permit has been issued, and you will have to queue at the immigration services at your point of entry into Canada to collect the study permit.


Note: when applying for a study permit, you must indicate the number of the designated educational institution (PST) of your university in Canada. You can find the PST for your institution on the following page: http://www.cic.gc.ca/francais/etudier/etudier-etablissements-liste.asp


  • Regarding the study permit, on the form to be completed (imm1294f) and to be provided on the Quebec immigration site, you are asked the level of study at this university: put 'University Baccalaureate'.


  • Upon receipt of the document, there you will also thoroughly check your number of Electronic Travel Authorization (AVE) appeared in the second paragraph of the second page. If it does not appear, you will have to make the request online via the following site: http://www.cic.gc.ca/francais/visiter/ave.asp The request is processed in 72 hours and the cost is $7.


  • Please note: obtaining the CAQ and Study Permit takes several months, which is why it is essential to start applying for the CAQ upon receipt of the letter of admission. In the absence of these documents, entry to the territory may be refused.


3. International insurance

You can find here some information about the health and hospitalization insurance from Laval University for international students


Enrolling in the health and hospitalization insurance plan for international students | Université Laval (ulaval.ca)


Basic social protection

There is a specific agreement between France and Quebec for basic social protection on site for students of French nationality. This agreement allows you to benefit from on-site support for your health expenses (up to the equivalent of French student social security).

The file will be to be created upon receipt of acceptance at the host university. The process can take several months. Proof of your affiliation with student social security in France will be required.


Before departure: You will need to ask your health insurance company for the necessary supporting documents and the SE 401-Q-106 form . This form, already completed by the international relations department, can be found in the media of your international relations intranet. You must then send it to the CPAM of your residence in order to have it signed. The validated form which will be returned to you by the CPAM will certify that you will be insured under the social security system in France and will allow your affiliation in Quebec. (NB: upon receipt of the form, remember to check the validity period which will have been indicated by the CPAM. Any form which will not cover you for the full duration of your stay will imply a renewal of the process during the year ) .


Upon arrival in Quebec: You will need to register with the Régie de l'assurance maladie du Québec (RAMQ) by submitting this form.

You will therefore be able to access RAMQ health care benefits and benefit from health and maternity insurance. In the event of a work accident or occupational disease, you will be covered by the Commission de la santé et de la sécurité du travail (CSST).

Please note: it will be important to present the RAMQ affiliation certificate to the Bureau du Registraire. Otherwise, the university will be legally required to bill you for its own international health insurance. Late fees may also be imposed on you if you do not send the affiliation certificate before the deadline given to you.


Social protection and complementary health


You must also take out international insurance (covering your medical and hospital costs on site, as well as repatriation). The market is quite open, among our privileged partners:

ACS, contact Sandra Zagzag: szagzag@acs-ami.com / 01.40.47.91.02

AVI, contact Afida Koucha: akoucha@avi-international.com/ 01.44.63.51.32

ISIS, contact Christine Barrat: christine.barrat@creassur-adc.com

Worldpass, contact : grady@worldpass.fr / 09 71 09 10 15 (promo code: 9EPITECH - allows you to benefit from a tariff reduction of 20%.)

Chapka, contact: info@chapka.fr / 01 74 85 50 50 (promo code: EPITECH10)


Make it clear to each contact that you are a student at EPITECH and that you will benefit from a preferential rate.


4. Help on arrival

If you arrive at Montréal-Trudeau airport in August (between August 4 and September 1), you can inquire about the "Accueil Plus" service, which allows you to reduce the waiting time for recover your study permit: http://www.accueilplus.ca/?lang=fr


Note: It is advisable to register on the French register established outside of France and to report to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs via the Ariane
accomodation:
University residences

You can book a room in a residence at: http://www.residences.ulaval.ca/

Please note, reservations must be made upon admission to Laval, contact: sres@sres.ulaval.ca


Note : The reservation is made from the start of the program. If you arrive before, you will be asked to pay an additional fee for each night you stay

For further information, see https://www.residences.ulaval.ca/futurs-residents/chambres-et-tarifs/


Off-campus accommodation :

If you prefer to live off campus, you can find ads at : https://www.bve.ulaval.ca/etudiants-etrangers/vivre-a-quebec/logement/logement-hors-campus/


Here are some basics about housing :

  • Housing division :

The number before the “½” indicates the number of rooms making up the accommodation and the “½” represents the bathroom. For example, for your family, explore the prices of housing types 4 ½ and 5 ½. Housing 4 ½ = 4 rooms (2 bedrooms, 1 kitchen and 1 living room) + 1 bathroom.

Housing 5 ½ = 5 rooms (3 bedrooms, 1 kitchen and 1 living room) + 1 bathroom.


  • Heating and electricity :

In the ad, if it says "n-ch, n-é" it means that neither heating nor electricity is included in the monthly payments and therefore that you will have to pay your electricity bill. You can therefore expect an additional 80$ to 120$ per month which will be added to your monthly fees.

Some units include heating and electricity, which means that the rent is fixed and includes these services.

Always ask the landlord if lighting and heating (electricity) costs are included in your rent.


  • Furniture :

In Quebec, a “semi-furnished” type apartment only includes a stove and a refrigerator (appliances). You will then need to find a table, a bed and other furniture.

It is very rare to find furnished apartments in Quebec.


  • Telecommunications :

In Quebec, telecommunication services operate on a flat rate basis and are usually the responsibility of the tenant.

You have to plan 100$ to 120$ per month for a basic trio.

The basic trios include a landline, internet connection and cable TV.

Telephone calls operate on a flat rate basis. Local calls are free, but long distance and overseas calls are charged.

Telecommunication services are much more expensive than in Europe and some cell phones in other countries do not work in Quebec.


A good piece of advice to give is to take an Airbnb on site before finding accommodation so that you can visit it in person (if you do not decide to stay on the Laval student campus). And beware of bus subscriptions between the north and south banks, know that it is much more expensive than in France.

courses:
Academic calendar

  • Fall semester: from the beginning of September to mid-December
  • Winter semester: from the beginning of January to the end of April


Take into account the possible course requirements for the next semester when you enroll for the first semester courses (which one you need to take on the 1st semester to be able to take one on the 2nd semester).


Program


Tailor-made certificate in information technology - diploma program (30 local credits), 1st cycle 


The program is made up of 21 local credits from block 1 (7 courses) in computer science (IFT and GLO) and 9 local credits (3 courses) of elective courses, ie 30 local credits over the year, therefore 15 local credits per session. Two distance learning courses are authorized per session.   


To obtain the diploma certificate, you must validate 30 local credits AND have a minimum average of 2*. Please note, the course requires a lot of personal work and few students manage to validate the certificate (around 20 to 25 percent generally speaking).


* The average of all your courses must be equal to or greater than 2. So, it is possible to obtain a D in a course, but still have a general average greater than 2 if the other grades are good. 

 

PLEASE NOTE: if you choose the diploma program, you cannot take master's level courses.


Credits

For EPITECH, if a student (diploma course) has obtained 12 local credits per session, i.e. 24 local credits, this is equivalent to 60 ECTS. However, if you have not obtained the 30 local credits required by Laval, you will not obtain the diploma.


Fall 

• Diploma program: take 5 classes (15 credits) 

Winter 

• Diploma program: take 5 classes (15 credits) 

 

Courses

You will have access to the following courses: 

• all IFT and GLO courses from 2000 to 5999   

• Management and Marketing courses and Organizational Information System. 1000 level 

• For those who take master's courses, they will have access to all the classes mentioned from 6000 except the following courses:   

IFT 7014 Directed Readings 

IFT 7026 Experimental project 

IFT 8002 Basic Knowledge Exam 

IFT 8003 Research project proposal 

IFT 8004 Thesis project proposal 

These courses are all 3 credits.


Please note: the course "GLO4001 introduction à la robotique" is complicated and requires a very good level in mathematics (theoretical mathematics).

Please note, for both programs, you are limited to 2 distance courses per session maximum.     

 

Concerning the preferences that are made in January, students must choose between taking the diploma program or not. Epitech will cover tuition fees in Laval to the extent of the credits required to obtain 60 ECTS credits. Any additional module you wish to follow will be at your expense.

You cannot change programs once there. 

Important: All courses are taught in French and theoretical. Presence in class compulsory, under penalty of loss of visa and repatriation to France at the student's expense (impact on credits). The courses are most likely more academic than at Epitech . 

The course list is given to you for information. It can change from year to year. If a course is not available when you arrive, EPITECH cannot be held responsible for it.
cost:
Estimated Budget :

Take into account you have a tuition fee for French & Belgian students or 15 000€ tuition fee for non-french & non belgian students.

Departure and costs relative to settling in : 

  • Paris - Quebec round trip flights (YQB) : around 800 euros (during back-to-school periods, the university sets up a shuttle system to the campus) 
  • CAQ :120 $ CA 
  • Study permit : 150 $ CA 
  • Adapted clothing for winter in Quebec : 500 $ CA 
  • Arrival (travel, temporary accommodation, restaurants) : 450 $ CA 
  • Moving in costs (housing equipment, deposits ...) : 600 $ CA 
  • University pass : 147.60 $CA per semester. It offers unlimited access to the regular services of the Capitale Transport Network (RTC) and the Société de transport de Lévis (STLévis), including the services of the Société des traversiers du Québec (Québec / Lévis), for Fall and Winter sessions. 

In total, about € 2,000 

You can also look here to get an idea of the budget. 


Living expenses : 

  • Accommodation on campus : from 382 $ CA /month without bedding and 550$ CA (for rooms in the largest houses) https://www.residences.ulaval.ca/futurs-residents/chambres-et-tarifs/ 


  • You can have access to an ethernet connection for 10 $CA/Month for 100 Go   

or Off-campus accommodation : count 500 $ CA/ month depending on the location and sharing of accommodation (the city center of Québec city can be really expensive) 


  • Food : 350 $ CA / month 

You should know that the bus network (including the ferry north of Quebec connecting old Quebec & Lévis) is maintained by two companies: one on the north shore (Quebec) & one on the south shore (Lévis). Paying just one of the two river banks is about 60$ a month (we have a reduction of 6$ thanks to Laval), paying both is more than 100$ a month. It is entirely possible to live on the south bank and pay only for the south bank : a single line goes up on the north bank & goes around the Laval campus. Without a monthly pass, the price of a trip (only one bus, no change) is 3.50$ per trip, whether on the north shore or the south shore. 


  • Telephone, Internet, etc. : 40 to 70$ CA / month 
  • Personal expenses, leisure, clothing, etc. : around 400 $/ month 
  • Books, school materials and furnitures : From 250$ to 450$ per semester depending on the courses taken. (Please note : a specific calculator can be requested). Certain subjects (in particular optional courses) require compulsory books (which are sometimes rarely used) which are quite expensive (over 100$ per book) and may be diffcult to find in time 
  • International medical insurance : 350$CA per semester for non-French students 
  • Edition of transcript : 10$ 


Please note : the university will offer you various medical, dental and other insurance options during your orientation week. If you do not wish to subscribe to it, you must let the university know. Otherwise these costs will be billed directly to you. They will not be supported by Epitech. 

These prices are for information only, they may vary.
